text: Property offenses account for 57,084 of the 70,003 reports at Boston’s 1989 peak.
The decline was already underway: 55,555 reports in 1993, 21% below 1989.
Operation Ceasefire began in 1996, targeting youth firearm violence.
editorialReason: Local violence-prevention initiative directly relevant to the topic; distinguish its narrow target from all crime.

text: By 2000, reported property crime was about half its 1989 level.
2003 · The Big Dig brings the Central Artery underground through downtown Boston.
editorialReason: A visible transformation of Boston’s geography locates this era; no crime-effect claim.

text: By 2010, violent index offenses numbered 5,819—55% below their 1989 count.
The FBI series ends at 20,110 reports—71% below the 1989 peak.
March 2020: Boston’s public-health emergency begins during the COVID-19 pandemic.
editorialReason: Local emergency marks the pandemic disruption; the chart does not establish its causal effect.

text: After the 2022 low of 27,537, the annual count rose to 31,239 in 2023.
